scenes.title: Becton Cleanroom Wafer Inspection Bay
scenes.reference_notes: Official instrument-operation photograph and labelled main-campus plan inspected. Photo shows a binocular inspection microscope beside a guided benchtop tool; plan distinguishes metrology, plasma, deposition, wet-process, lithography, entry and gowning bays. The pictured manual handling arrangement is represented by a three-axis motorized mechanical surrogate; exact model, dimensions and placement on the source floor plan are not known.
observed_cues: Upright binocular inspection head over a flat workpiece fixture.
Orange workpiece handling supports and an open worktop.
Cleanroom surroundings; official floor plan distinguishes the metrology zone.
scenes.reconstruction_scope: A local metrology bay; not the full Becton cleanroom or a surveyed floorplan.

equipment.role: Binocular microscope head and articulated wafer fixture
equipment.evidence: photo-informed exterior, estimated scale and mechanism

layout_evidence.supports: Local microscope/fixture form or cleanroom zoning; no measured registration of the photograph to the plan.
Local microscope/fixture form or cleanroom zoning; no measured registration of the photograph to the plan.

layout_rationale: Retain a broad open-frame inspection worktop and operator aisle.
Keep the stereo head over the wafer stage with a grounded bench and continuous column.
Room perimeter and entry are estimated context; do not merge unphotographed cleanroom process rooms.

circulation.operator_approach: Front and left aisle to the inspection fixture.
circulation.service_access: Rear bench service strip; authored clearance, not certification.

task.name: Position a wafer coupon for visual inspection
task.description: Move the clamped inert coupon in XY and adjust the head height; inspect joint and specimen poses.
task.observable: stage_x, stage_y, focus_height and wafer_coupon pose.

limitations: Exterior and travel are authored estimates, not manufacturer CAD or institution-approved dimensions.
No microscope image formation, scientific wafer metrology or cleanroom process simulation.
Source images remain external references; redistribution rights and institutional endorsement are not established.

scenes.title: Ferguson Structural Test Hall
scenes.institution: University of Texas at Austin — Ferguson Structural Engineering Laboratory
scenes.reference_notes: Official wide interior photograph inspected: tall long-span hall with red reaction portals, horizontal concrete beam specimens, overhead yellow gantry crane, large strong-floor work area and high side windows. The official site identifies a structural research facility at Pickle Research Campus. The portal, loading stroke and sensor rail are original mechanical estimates. No structural response or actual FSEL controller is reproduced.
observed_cues: Multiple red steel reaction portals aligned along a long high-bay hall
Full-size concrete beams on supports and loading heads
Yellow overhead bridge crane beneath high side windows and exposed services
scenes.reconstruction_scope: Photo-informed multi-bay high hall; dimensions and experiment layout estimated.

support.evidence: Portal feet and beam cribs contact z=0; crib caps continuously support the slab.

equipment.role: Large reaction portal, inert slab and sensor traverse
equipment.evidence: photo-informed exterior; authored loading approach and sensor motion

layout_evidence.supports: Red reaction portals, long concrete slabs, high service rails, overhead yellow crane and side aisles.

layout_rationale: Preserve the high hall and two longitudinal test bays.
Keep the primary slab supported on two full-height cribbed piers and the portal independently grounded.
Retain side access aisles and overhead structural rails; estimates are not surveyed FSEL dimensions.

circulation.operator_approach: Left/front aisle, outside the static test specimen and reaction posts.
circulation.service_access: Wide side aisles; no building-code or full machinery-safety certification.

task.name: Approach a structural specimen and position its inspection head
task.description: Move a rigid loading platen toward an inert beam and translate the observation head along it.
task.observable: load_ram, sensor_traverse, loading_platen and beam_specimen poses.

limitations: Hall, beam, frame and mechanical travel dimensions are estimates from a single official photograph.
The beam remains rigid; no hydraulic loading physics, strain, fracture, concrete damage or calibrated load-cell output.
Source images remain external references; no institutional endorsement or media release permission established.

scenes.title: Richmond 64 m Towing Tank Hall
scenes.institution: University of California, Berkeley — FLOW Lab
scenes.reference_notes: Official laboratory facility page identifies the 64 m towing/wave tank at Richmond Field Station; its interior photo shows the tank, carriage rails and service aisle. Tank clear length, width and depth are published. Shed, carriage, attachment and service-floor elevation are estimated; the 8 m positioning window is a mechanical demonstrator.
observed_cues: A very long open tank occupies most of a narrow corrugated-metal shed.
Parallel tank-side rails and hanging looped supply cables follow the entire experiment axis.
A narrow right-side walkway contains service consoles under exposed roof trusses and fluorescent luminaires.
scenes.reconstruction_scope: Full published tank envelope in an estimated long shed, with a local carriage demonstration window.

support.evidence: Continuous tank foundation and solid service platform rest at z=0; carriage wheels seat on full-length wall rails.

equipment.role: 64 m tank envelope, supported carriage and rigid mounted model
equipment.evidence: published tank dimensions; photograph-informed and estimated secondary geometry

layout_evidence.supports: Long narrow tank shed, exposed roof members, wall corrugations, looped cable services and right-side operator walkway.

layout_rationale: Preserve the 64 m long axis and source-published 2.40 m width / 1.80 m clear depth.
Keep the model carriage spanning the tank rails and the operator route on the right.
A raised service datum and access steps are authored to reconcile the above-floor model with waist-height viewing; actual tank embedment is unknown.

circulation.operator_approach: Front steps to the right-side elevated service walkway.
circulation.service_access: Long right-side route; no egress, guardrail or accessibility compliance claim.

task.name: Position a mounted hydrodynamic test model
task.description: Move the carriage through an 8 m demonstration window and adjust the rigid model mounting height.

limitations: The water surface is visual only; no buoyancy, drag, waves or fluid measurements are calculated.
Tank dimensions are documented, while the shed, walkway datum, carriage form, end absorber and stroke are estimated.
The scene does not reproduce published maximum carriage speed or scientific accuracy.
Source media remain external references and no institutional approval or reuse license is established.

scenes.title: EDL Electrochemical Test Workbench
scenes.institution: Carnegie Mellon University — Electrochemical Decarbonization Laboratory
scenes.reference_notes: Official facility photos show the electrochemical test bench and wider experimental lab; visible nameplates identify an 850e fuel-cell test system and 850BP pressure-control unit. Cabinet sizes, dry specimen fixture and its actuation are original estimates. The wider lab photograph informs furnishings, not a measured registration of benches.
observed_cues: Tall 850e cabinet and shorter gauge-covered 850BP unit occupy the grey worktop beside a restrained cylinder rack.
White tubing and thick electrical leads connect bench hardware beneath an overhead utility shelf.
The wider room has pale wood base cabinets, a large end-of-island sink and stainless drying pegboard.
scenes.reconstruction_scope: Local testbench and nearby sink/cylinder furnishings in an estimated room.

equipment.role: Photo-informed tester cabinets and articulated inert-coupon fixture
equipment.evidence: visible 850e/850BP styling; dimensions and dry-fixture control are estimated

layout_evidence.supports: Tester face details, white tubing, restrained cylinders, pale wood base cabinets, overhead utility shelf or sink/pegboard island.
Tester face details, white tubing, restrained cylinders, pale wood base cabinets, overhead utility shelf or sink/pegboard island.

layout_rationale: Keep the compact tester/pressure-control pair on a grounded wide workbench.
Add the distinct restrained cylinder rack and a sink island with drying pegs.
Furniture identity follows two official photos; relative bench placement and room perimeter remain authored estimates.

circulation.operator_approach: Front aisle between the dry coupon fixture and sink island.
circulation.service_access: Right side access around the restrained cylinders; no gas-system or layout compliance certification.

task.name: Access an inert electrochemical specimen fixture
task.description: Translate the dry sample drawer and open its perimeter clamp while observing the dummy coupon pose.

limitations: 850e/850BP exterior styling is identifiable, but all dimensions and the articulated dry fixture are estimates.
No fuel, gas, pressure, electrical current, reaction products or electrochemical scientific response is simulated.
The example fixture does not reproduce an OEM test protocol or equipment controller.
Reference photographs remain external and have no verified redistribution license; no institutional endorsement.
